phases.label: Foundation
phases.blurb: A cash-market screen, a first look at call transcripts, and a pipeline that had to be repaired before it could be trusted.

phases.label: Identity and calls
phases.blurb: The page gets a name, a call library and its first exchange trackers. Most of the commits in this stretch are transcript batches.

phases.label: Scanners and personal tools
phases.blurb: Breakout bases, a watchlist, a results calendar and a management-outlook row: the page starts to fit how it is actually used.

phases.label: Outside the exchange
phases.blurb: Weather, power generation and power prices as demand signals, and a scheduler that no longer depends on GitHub's clock.

phases.label: Short ideas and trackers
phases.blurb: Price-action screens for the short side, a banks-and-NBFC dashboard, and more careful exchange tracking.

phases.label: The patterns era
phases.blurb: Corporate actions corrected at the source, then chart patterns, replayed against history to see whether any of it works.

phases.label: Efficiency and a front page
phases.blurb: Faster builds and a lighter page, a landing page, three years of history, and rules tightened after looking at real charts.

nodes.title: Cash Accumulation Watch
nodes.what: The first screen: F&O stocks that close higher and above their moving averages while delivered shares rise and single-stock-futures open interest falls.
nodes.insight: The idea that shaped everything after it: delivery, not just price, as the signal, and open interest as the check on whether positions are being closed or built.

nodes.title: Moving-average context and F&O call intelligence
nodes.what: Moving averages on every stock, and the first analysis of earnings-call transcripts for F&O names, with the selected F&O transcripts handled first.
nodes.insight: Transcripts became a second data source next to prices, and the forward-looking parts of a call (outlook, guidance) turned out to be the part worth keeping.

nodes.title: The daily workflow repaired
nodes.what: Three quick fixes in a row: the workflow file itself, source files that had been uploaded damaged, and manual builds that now run immediately.
nodes.insight: A page that updates itself is only worth anything if the update runs. The pipeline kept needing attention until the scheduler rework a week later.

nodes.title: BSE Exchange Tracker
nodes.what: BSE options premium turnover in rupees, compared with the same weekday and the same window in earlier periods.
nodes.insight: Comparing a Friday with other Fridays removed most of the noise: single-day turnover swings by multiples around expiries.

nodes.title: Branded Rachit's Market Lens
nodes.what: The dashboard gets its name, and the end-of-day screens and transcript coverage are upgraded.
nodes.insight: From here the page is treated as a product with one reader, not a collection of scripts.

nodes.title: Conference call summary library
nodes.what: Every analysed call in one place, with the management outlook, what analysts pressed on, and the key risks.
nodes.insight: The library grew by dozens of small batches over the next few days. Reading a call's outlook in thirty seconds replaced reading the transcript.

nodes.title: An unofficial transcript removed
nodes.what: The Sona Comstar analysis was pulled because its source was not an official exchange transcript.
nodes.insight: The first rule set for data: if the source is not official, it does not go on the page, however useful the content looks.

nodes.title: A week of exchange-tracker polish
nodes.what: Three-column layout, equal panels, compact chart headers, and cash selling highlighted in recent activity.
nodes.insight: Around eight small pull requests for one tab: its design was settled by looking at it, not planned in advance.

nodes.title: MCX options turnover and week buckets
nodes.what: The same tracker for MCX, combined with BSE under one tab, with week-of-month buckets and a 6 AM IST refresh.
nodes.insight: MCX publishes late, so it got its own morning refresh. That is why the daily workflow still has a separate early run.

nodes.title: Fresh 52-week highs
nodes.what: Stocks making new 52-week highs, with delivery context.
nodes.insight: Market-cap bands followed on 30 Oct, to separate a new high in a large cap from one in a small cap.

nodes.title: Signal Confluence
nodes.what: Stocks flagged by several delivery-based screens at once.
nodes.insight: Archived on 21 Nov and kept in the code; the agreement between screens now lives in Short Ideas.

nodes.title: Forward-only transcript batches
nodes.what: Around two dozen batches of transcript analysis, restricted to what management said about the future.
nodes.insight: About a third of the pull requests up to 1 Nov were transcript batches, which is why the early history looks so busy: the work was content, not code.

nodes.title: Market-cap filters, and a unit bug caught
nodes.what: Top 500 by market cap and five market-cap bands for the call and 52-week-high lists.
nodes.insight: A unit conversion in NSE's market-cap file was wrong and fixed the same day. The loader now checks the unit in the file's header instead of assuming it.

nodes.title: F&O breakout base scanner
nodes.what: Stocks in the upper quarter of a valid 40, 60 or 90-session base, with toggleable quality filters.
nodes.insight: Tightened the same day: the range limit went down to 10% and the 120-session window was dropped, because longer bases were mostly drift, not consolidation.

nodes.title: Watchlist
nodes.what: A star on every stock, a Watchlist subtab, and a watchlist-only filter. It lives in the browser, with export and import to move it between devices.
nodes.insight: Later features report to it: the pattern digest and the Today page list new flags on starred stocks.

nodes.title: Base Follow-Through
nodes.what: Every past session's base scan replayed, recording what happened after each signal.
nodes.insight: The first time the page tested one of its own ideas against history. It set the habit: no scan ships without a replay.

nodes.title: Password lock, and sub-tabs
nodes.what: The page can be encrypted behind a password, and several tabs are folded into sub-tabs.
nodes.insight: Made off by default on 3 Nov. It is still there when it is needed, but it costs a click every time it is on.

nodes.title: Results calendar
nodes.what: Every announced result meeting, an Upcoming Results subtab, and a 'result in N days' banner on the stock chart.
nodes.insight: A small feature that answers 'is there a result coming?' right on the chart, before anything else does.

nodes.title: Management outlook row
nodes.what: A six-label outlook (bullish to bearish) above the chart, and guidance cuts and raises that no longer get silently dropped when a batch changes shape.
nodes.insight: The second change is the more important one: a parser that quietly ignores an unfamiliar field is worse than one that fails.

nodes.title: BSE delivery missing for the first nine days of a month
nodes.what: BSE writes the date as a number, so 2 November arrives as 2112026 and the leading zero was lost. Delivery for days 1 to 9 was being dropped.
nodes.insight: The fix also made the build retry every 30 minutes from 7 PM IST until the day's BSE delivery is complete, instead of publishing with NSE-only delivery.

nodes.title: Temperatures and power generation
nodes.what: City temperatures against history as a proxy for cooling and heating demand, and all-India power generation from the CEA's daily reports.
nodes.insight: Experimental from the start: whether weather and generation lead listed power and cooling stocks was left as a question, not a claim.

nodes.title: SQLite store dropped
nodes.what: An unused database was deleted and the fetcher's user agent renamed.
nodes.insight: Plain files in the cache were enough. Fewer moving parts to restore on a fresh runner.

nodes.title: A scheduler that does not depend on GitHub's clock
nodes.what: A Cloudflare Worker starts the workflow at 6:00–7:00 IST mornings and 19:00–22:00 IST weekday evenings. GitHub's own schedule stays as a backstop that skips quickly when a build already covered it.
nodes.insight: GitHub's scheduled runs had started hours late or not at all. The page being on time matters more than the page being clever.

nodes.title: Company-focused power view
nodes.what: Power generation by company (NTPC, Adani Power, Adani Green, NHPC, JSW Energy) with a fixed six-city temperature grid.
nodes.insight: Regions and states were dropped in favour of companies: the reader cares about the stocks.

nodes.title: Candlestick chart, run-rate estimates and IEX prices
nodes.what: The stock chart becomes candlesticks, company generation gets monthly and quarterly run-rate estimates, and IEX day-ahead prices are added.
nodes.insight: The run-rate estimate is the earliest version of a question that is still open: how much of a month's number can you read from part of it.

nodes.title: A backtest, run locally
nodes.what: NHPC scored against all-India hydro generation, shown as small panels in the power view.
nodes.insight: Run on a laptop, not in the build: backtests download prices, and the build never should.

nodes.title: Short Ideas: six price-action screens, with a replay
nodes.what: Cash selling, laggards, breakdown, rejected at the 50-day, short build-up and near 52-week low, each with a replay of what followed, and a chart for every flagged stock.
nodes.insight: Each screen shows its replay beside it, with the caveat that it is a sanity check on a few hundred sessions in one market regime, not a backtest.

nodes.title: Any weekday, any window
nodes.what: Pick a weekday and a window for BSE and MCX, with the daily read moved below the first row of charts.
nodes.insight: Turnover is dominated by expiry days. Letting the reader choose the weekday is how that stops being a surprise.

nodes.title: Credit Desk: banks and NBFC dashboards
nodes.what: Two sector dashboards embedded with a vendored Chart.js and no external requests. Renamed Peer Radar on 21 Nov.
nodes.insight: Vendored so the page keeps working offline and never loads a third-party script.

nodes.title: Bonuses and splits straight from NSE
nodes.what: Corporate actions now come from NSE's own feed instead of only being inferred from price jumps.
nodes.insight: City Union Bank's 1:3 bonus was missed by the price detector and its chart showed a 21% crash. The exchange publishes the ratio, so the page uses it.

nodes.title: Technical Patterns
nodes.what: Ascending and descending triangles and rectangles, found from swing highs and lows on adjusted prices, with a flat level that has to be touched at least three times.
nodes.insight: On simulated random price paths the same rules still find a pattern in about four paths in ten. The page says that on its face.

nodes.title: Signal Confluence archived
nodes.what: The tab is kept in the code but no longer built or shown.
nodes.insight: A tab that overlaps a better one is a cost every time the page is read. Bringing it back is one line.

nodes.title: Two years of history and weekly pattern scans
nodes.what: History deepens from fourteen months to two years, filled in gradually so no single run has to fetch it all. Patterns are scanned on weekly candles too.
nodes.insight: Longer patterns need longer history. This is the first of three steps that ended at three years.

nodes.title: Patterns on the stock page get their own charts
nodes.what: Each pattern is drawn on a side chart with its breakout, shape and target instead of lines over the main chart.
nodes.insight: Lines on the main chart hid the candles they were describing.

nodes.title: Bases and Shorts move in; breaks are replayed
nodes.what: Breakout Bases and Short Ideas become sub-tabs of Technical Patterns. NEW and JUST BROKE markers, a digest of what changed, a 0–5 conviction score, and a replay of past breaks at 20, 40 and 60 sessions.
nodes.insight: The first replay put numbers on the question. Delivery on the break session itself, not on the day the pattern was noticed, became the measure.

nodes.title: Trade-for-trade stocks, renamed stocks, untraded days
nodes.what: Stocks in the BE and BZ series keep their volume as delivery, renamed stocks are stitched by ISIN, and the last price carries through untraded sessions.
nodes.insight: Found by a stock that was simply missing from the page. Gaps in the data show up as missing stocks, not wrong numbers, which is why they are easy to miss.

nodes.title: Faster builds, with proof
nodes.what: Pattern scans vectorised (72% of the pattern scan's time had been one function) and the breakout-base signal made incremental.
nodes.insight: Each speed-up was checked to give exactly the same answers as the original on real data before it replaced it.

nodes.title: A lighter page: heavy tabs and stock data on demand
nodes.what: Heavy tabs and each stock's price arrays are loaded the first time they are opened.
nodes.insight: Measured on a CPU slowed four times, like a mid-range phone: load 4.7s to 2.3s, DOM nodes 128,000 to 8,600, memory 58MB to 22MB. The download did not shrink; the work after it did.

nodes.title: A first Today page
nodes.what: High-delivery breaks, new short ideas, cash accumulation, fresh bases and watchlist flags together.
nodes.insight: Tables only. It became a landing page the next day.

nodes.title: Daily alerts built, then removed
nodes.what: An alerts feature (watchlist flags raised as GitHub issues) was built and then taken out before shipping, in favour of the Today page.
nodes.insight: Dropped when the Today page was chosen instead: a page you open is a simpler home for 'what is new' than notifications to manage.

nodes.title: Touches have to be a gap apart
nodes.what: Swing highs a few bars apart are one test of a level, not two. Two touches are enough when they are at least 60 sessions apart.
nodes.insight: It dropped 42 of 212 patterns, five of them fresh breaks. Replayed afterwards, high delivery on the break gave no reliable edge on any pattern.

nodes.title: Three years of history
nodes.what: About 710 sessions instead of 512, with older corporate actions fetched once.
nodes.insight: Extending history exposed an unadjusted bonus (MOTILALOFS, 3:1) and a BSE file with a differently spelled column. Both fixed; the page now sees a level tested three years ago.

nodes.title: Today becomes a landing page
nodes.what: A headline, three charts worth a look, BSE, MCX and power activity side by side, short ideas, one call, and everything else new.
nodes.insight: From tables to a page that reads like a briefing: the numbers are the same, the order is the argument.

nodes.title: MCX missing from the stock search
nodes.what: NSE's half-yearly market-cap ranking omits some stocks that are in the Nifty 500 and F&O lists. Those are now added to the default universe.
nodes.insight: The default list went from 1,000 to 1,017. The source file, not the page, was the gap.

nodes.title: 200DMA retest
nodes.what: Stocks that closed under the 200-day average on high delivery, fell away, and came back to retest it, across every liquid share with an F&O filter.
nodes.insight: Its replay showed a small edge for all shares (about 0.4 points against Nifty over ten sessions) and almost none within F&O, and the page shows both.

nodes.title: Nifty trend flag
nodes.what: A banner and a mark on fresh breakouts when Nifty is below its 50 or 100-day average.
nodes.insight: Split by the market's state, breakouts showed no real difference; breakdowns did worse when Nifty was already weak. The flag is a caution, not a filter.

nodes.title: Earlier touches made visible
nodes.what: A pattern whose flat level was tested before the chart starts now shows a dashed level and a whole-history strip.
nodes.insight: The count was right and the picture could not show it. A number the reader cannot see on the chart is a number they have to take on trust.

nodes.title: This timeline
nodes.what: How the page evolved, from the first screen to the latest change, read from a curated file plus the repository's own history.
nodes.insight: New changes appear here as nodes: automatically from merged pull requests, and in more detail when the story is written up.

nodes.title: Sector clusters
nodes.what: When several stocks of the same kind of business (life insurers, private banks, cement) are near a breakout or through one together, it is called out on Today, on the Breakout Bases cards and on each stock's own page, with the group's delivery alongside.
nodes.insight: NSE's broad industries were too coarse (Financial Services holds banks, insurers and brokers together), so groups are hand-kept in config/sector_groups.csv. On the 20 Nov data, 19 groups had three or more candidates; the life insurers were five.

nodes.title: A copy-and-paste table for 52-week highs
nodes.what: A Copy Table sub-tab with two plain tables, F&O names and non-F&O names, each with its own copy button: last price, one-day change, and the distance from the 52-week high and from the 50-day average.
nodes.insight: The charts are for reading; these are for taking the list somewhere else. An all-time-high column was built and dropped: the desk holds three years of history, so it would have understated the distance for stocks whose real peak is older.

nodes.title: A 52-week high has to close above every prior close
nodes.what: A stock that touches a new 52-week high intraday but closes under any earlier close in the 252-session window no longer counts.
nodes.insight: On the 20 Nov data the rule dropped 5 of 22 names (Coforge, Phoenix Mills, Fluorochem, LIC Housing Finance, DCB Bank), 3 of them in F&O. A new high that closes back inside the old range is a failed attempt, not a breakout.

nodes.title: NSE options tracker
nodes.what: A third exchange next to BSE and MCX: all NSE options premium turnover, equity options on their own (index and single-stock, with the split by month), and commodity options, from NSE's own daily bhavcopies. History from January 2024. The charts plot NSE's own share price (listed on BSE from 24 Sep 2026), not Nifty. A small panel in the commodity view gives NSE commodity options' share of NSE plus MCX commodity option premium over a rolling three months.
nodes.insight: Commodity options trade almost only around expiry: over the last three full months, 66% of NSE commodity option premium came on expiry day and the session before it, and crude oil carried nearly all of it. The commodity view tracks those two sessions for every expiry and the month's cumulative turnover. Against MCX, NSE commodity options have grown from 0.4% to 3.0% of the combined premium turnover (rolling three months, to 30 Oct).

nodes.title: Open interest on expiry days
nodes.what: Single-stock-futures open interest no longer counts the contract that expires on the session: NSE's file still lists it with the open interest it had going into the close, although it is settled to zero. A continuity audit over every F&O stock and session, oi_audit.py, was added.
nodes.insight: Blue Star showed 51.9 lakh shares on its 23 Nov expiry day and 38.8 lakh two sessions later, a 25% drop; without the expiring series the 23 Nov total is 39.1 lakh and the change is 1%. Across the 42 monthly expiries held, 7,056 stock-sessions were affected, and the next-session change was overstated as a drop by more than 10 points in 28% of them. The real drop now shows on the expiry day itself.

nodes.title: NSE tracker blank on the live site
nodes.what: The NSE view was empty after the first live build: on a build server with no cache the tracker's date column came out as plain objects, a newer pandas then refused it, and the failure was swallowed. The dates are now always datetimes, a test builds the tracker with no cache at all, and a failure now shows its reason on the page.
nodes.insight: The tracker had only ever been built where its cache files already existed. A fresh runner exposed the gap, which is why a cold-start test now exists.

nodes.title: Ranges: a stricter rectangle, judged as a trade
nodes.what: A new sub-tab beside the old Rectangle one (which is untouched): a horizontal range whose breaking boundary has three touches, with touches that alternate between the sides, closes that cross the middle, and a trade plan (entry, stop at the middle, measured-move target, prior trend). Every past break is replayed as a trade in R against the old rectangle scan.
nodes.insight: On 1,901 past breaks the new ranges had an expectancy between -0.07R and +0.02R per trade in the large groups, an average win of at most 1.4R and at most 3% of trades reaching 4R: no sign of the asymmetry that a 35-45% win rate needs. Daily breakdowns taken to the measured move did best, at +0.13R on 922 trades. The old rectangle finds far fewer breaks (68 up and 119 down on the daily scan against 562 and 927).
